# Record 1 points at a commit that no longer exists

`harness start` ran while this branch was accidentally based on SEEN-088's branch, because a checkout
to main had failed: graphify's post-commit hook leaves `graphify-out` dirty, and git refuses to
switch branches over uncommitted changes. The branch was rebased onto main afterwards, which rewrote
the commit record 1 recorded as its head.

So record 1's `head` and `base_commit` name `a228b86`, which is not reachable any more. The chain is
intact and nothing else is affected; the anchor is simply stale. Recorded here rather than by
rewriting record 1, which is the one thing a journal must never do.

The underlying nuisance is worth naming: after every commit the graph rebuilds in the background, so
a branch switch immediately afterwards fails. Discarding `graphify-out` before switching is the
workaround, and a cleaner answer belongs with SEEN-089's delivery checks.
